subject.gist: Track coaches Matt and Cristina build without borrowing, live in an RV during construction, and embrace outdoor cooking despite Cristina’s doubts about the cold.

story.text: Matt and Cristina are track coaches who leave expensive island housing behind and learn to build their own home. They live in an RV while saving for each load of timber, accepting help and learning as they go. Matt wants a house that does not feel like a box, with room for their art and views into the forest. Cristina initially finds the outdoor kitchen and shower hard to accept, especially in the cold. They still have limited electricity and no working refrigerator, but their garden keeps expanding, and she calls this the dream she never had.

features.title: Rainforest household clearing
features.description: Matt and Cristina chose this one-acre [0.40-hectare] rainforest property in Fern Forest because they could afford to own land outright after finding Maui too expensive. Matt describes it as backing onto a forest reserve at the end of the road, and credits the surrounding forest and slower pace with helping him sleep more deeply. Kirsten's account gives the land purchase as $22,000 in 2019 and the combined land-and-house cost as roughly $60,000, while linking local affordability to volcanic hazard exposure.
features.unknown: Parcel and reserve boundaries are not surveyed. The description links affordability to volcanic hazard, without a site-specific risk assessment.
